utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Having started at this time, our next break will be -- our first break will be at 1640 hours, for half an hour. Thereafter, we'll see how we go. Yes. It's cross-examination. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Witness A. This is the third day that I'm beginning the day by cross-examining you. I told the Trial Chamber that I will continue to examine you on the same topic for not more than ten minutes, and in order to accomplish that, I will ask that you give me very specific and brief answers. But before we continue with the topic where we left off, let me ask you a question that my client expressly wanted me to ask you. When you were in Sid, waiting to cross the exchange line, what were you telling Mr. Tadic regarding Stevan Todorovic? If you remember, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what I was telling him regarding Stevan Todorovic. Whatever I might have been saying, if I was saying anything at all, it certainly wasn't anything positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After you crossed into the territory controlled by the HVO, did you see then, or later on, Pero Vicentic, who has a nickname Konj? Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him, but not really well. I met him approximately one year after my exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to go back to the last topic we broached, concerning your conversation with Mr. Franjo Barukcic. You testified to this before this Chamber on the 8th of July, on page 10759. You gave a detailed interview to the investigators of the OTP which lasted for ten days in 1994. You confirmed that during my last cross-examination. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During that interview, you repeated the name of Mr. Tadic several times, just as you repeated the name of Mr. Barukcic several times. And on page 10 of B/C/S version, and page 9 of English version, you mentioned the same names mentioned in paragraph 47 of the statement that is in front of you now, which is a 92 bis statement. I will now read out to you what you said in that statement in 1994 regarding your transfer to the TO: "When I arrived in there, there were 10 to 15 prisoners there, including Luka Gregurevic, Ivica Evic, Mato Senic, and Cutura, who was on duty with Luka during the first night of the attack. I saw that Luka's pants were slit in the area of the hips and that his face was swollen. Kemal Akic was there as well, Esad Cosic, Franjo Barukcic, Salko Hurtic also wearing the uniform of a reserve policeman, Ibrahim Salkic, Ibela, and Dzevad Jusufovic, Ilija Mandic and Anto Orsolic were in the room as well." Do you remember stating that in 1994 and signing your statement then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You never mentioned in that statement that Barukcic had allegedly told you that Tadic arrested him in his house?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like for the Prosecutor to confirm to me whether in your 1994 statement this is mentioned anywhere, namely, that this witness claimed that Barukcic had told him that he had been arrested by Tadic in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: My learned friend did ask me to do this. I regret that I haven't quite done it yet. I think Mr. Lukic is probably right. Could I just be given a moment to quickly go through the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to speed up the proceedings and not ask the witness to read his entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- quite right. I think it's wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then, in your 1994 statement, when giving it, you talked to the investigators for four full days, and your memory must have been more fresh than it is now, and you mentioned Mr. Barukcic several times, and Mr. Tadic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you talked again to the Prosecutor and the investigators on the 12th of July, 2001, in Odzak. When we -- when I interrogated you yesterday, you said that that was mostly an informative interview, but on that occasion you also did not mention what Mr. Barukcic had told you. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your second interview with the Prosecutor, which took place in July of 2001, in Odzak, and you described this interview as an informative one to me yesterday, did you on that occasion mention to them that Barukcic had told you that he had been arrested by Tadic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think I could indicate that I've been through the statement, and I can't find any reference by the witness to Mr. Tadic arresting Mr. Barukcic, in the 1994 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness A, do you know what happened to Franjo Barukcic after you were exchanged? Because you were exchanged before him. So do you know what happened to him afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Barukcic was exchanged after me, and he came in a very bad shape. I met him once or twice very briefly, because at that time I myself spent most of my time at home and in hospitals. He lived somewhere from Slavonia, near the Hungarian border, so that he was not near me. I also know that he died some two or three years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I know too. So at any rate, he died after you were giving your statement in 1994; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He died after 1994. I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that room where you stayed with Barukcic, there were only the two of you when he told you that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before you were transferred into that room, during your previous incarceration, you were always in a larger group, where there were more than one person with you; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And he never told you this story in the presence of another inmate or another person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not able and we did not dare discuss anything, let alone this topic, and we only discussed it once there were only two of us in the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that on that critical day when he was arrested, he was in the house of his neighbour, where other neighbours from that neighbourhood took shelter too? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him saying that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he by any chance tell you that on that occasion his son Nikola was also arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never told me anything about his son's, Nikola's, arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he perhaps, during your conversation, tell you that he had known that his son Nikola was exchanged in the first exchange that took place in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness A, you were arrested by the policemen and the specials from Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "arrest." Do you mean in my apartment or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, who took you to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken in a Golf vehicle belonging to Josip Orsolic by Miljkovic Slobodan, called Lugar, and Stankovic Nebojsa, called Cera. These two people took me to the duty service of the MUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already told us that. That's all I'm interested in. Do you know whether these two persons that you mentioned were members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim with certainty. Miljkovic definitely was not. As for Nebojsa Stankovic, called Cera, I'm not sure whether he was or was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Sulejman Tihic was also arrested by the policemen and specials from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is what Sulejman Tihic told me at the time, which is that at the time when he was arrested, he was with the attorney Borislav Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the specials from Serbia arrested Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the specials from Serbia and the policemen arrested also Coner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, it's only a minor point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The way the question is framed and the answer comes out, the way it's translated, you just don't know what the witness means. The question: "Do you know that the specials from Serbia arrested Izet Izetbegovic?" Answer: "No." Is that "no, they did not arrest him" or "no, I don't know"? I don't want to split hairs, but if it ever becomes important, you won't be able to tell from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, perhaps that can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know who arrested Izet Izetbegovic. You don't know about that, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that they were arrested and brought in. I don't know who brought them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that Tihic and Izetbegovic and Coner were high officials of the SDA, as was Omer Nalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the first two ones, perhaps; and as for Coner and Omer Nalic, I don't think that they were high officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you certainly know that Franjo Barukcic was a high official of the HDZ. He was that party's secretary.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Barukcic was a member of the HDZ. I used to see him going to the HDZ premises. Now as to his exact function, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in 2001, you remembered and said to the Prosecution that the man told you -- the man who had died in the meantime told you, when you were alone, that he had been arrested by Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only told me that Brko came to get him and took him. He didn't tell me how he got there or how was that done. He simply told me, "Miro, Brko came to get me."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness A. I am Pantelic, an attorney representing Blagoje Simic. In view of your long experience as a security officer, and in view of many functions you held in the past, and in view of the fact that you discussed this with the Prosecution in 1994, would you agree with me that in the time period before 1992, the public security station in Samac was subordinated to an organisation above it? Can you tell us what organisation was that in that police hierarchy? Was that regional, SUP, or what was that higher office called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina; then the next level down was the centre of public Security Services. There were several of them. Samac was in the jurisdiction of the centre of the public security services of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And did a similar structure exist in the police organs after you were exchanged and began working in Orasje, in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Was there a similar or identical organisational structure there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, when I crossed to the territory of Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, there was a different organisational structure. Conditions were different. The war was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And since you were in Orasje, can you tell us whether there was a higher police structure, a higher police instance in relation to that one in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were police stations throughout that free territory, and above them was the ministry of the canton -- or the ministry of the county, that was in charge of that area, and then naturally there was the government, which for a certain period of time had its seat in Mostar; and then later on the Federation's government moved to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about how the chain of command functioned in Republika Srpska from 1992 through to 1995? Did they have the same kind of hierarchy, if you know, in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that I know anything about that. I wouldn't like to speculate and base my answers on what I have heard. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us: When was the Croatian community of Bosnian Posavina [Realtime transcript read in error"Bosnia and Posavina"] established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what kind of community do you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Herceg-Bosna, and it is a well-known fact that the Croatian people in Bosnia had those communities. You said that you were in Orasje, which was part of Herceg-Bosna, and now I'm asking you if you know when the Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina was established.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a small intervention, correction in transcript. When I made the reference to Bosanski Posavina, it was two times --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Page 10, line 3, and page 9, line 23. In fact, it was maybe an error in interpretation. It should read "Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina," not Bosnia and Posavina, but Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Bosnian Posavina, all right. It will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I just want to say that there was no such thing. There was the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and it lasted -- it was in existence in those places where the HVO members were. I don't know about any other community.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the area of Odzak, there was an HVO unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was exchanged, I don't know whether it was then or after a certain period of time that Odzak was under the control of the Serb forces. I don't know what was going on during the time while I was detained, but it is probably not in dispute that at that time in Odzak there were members of the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At any rate, when you were in Orasje discharging your functions, the Croatian Defence Council was present there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are aware of a military operation carried out by the Republika Srpska army in Krajina in late June 1992, which was entitled The Corridor. That was its name. Are you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not cross from Croatia to Bosnia and Herzegovina across the River Sava. Perhaps only a year -- it was only after a year I was exchanged that I did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. But let's say from the time when you crossed and until today, have you heard of that operation that was carried out in Posavina by the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did hear a thing or two. I know that there was this corridor, and I know that some operations were conducted there. Some of the territory was taken by the Serbs. Serbs did take some territory away from the HVO. But as regards to the town itself, the military and the HVO, really, I wasn't interested in it at all and I'm not at all familiar with this whole issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You do know of the village of Gornica, in the territory of the new municipality of Bosanski Samac, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You probably know, so you can tell me whether it is a predominant -- it is predominantly inhabited by Croats.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it did have a Croatian majority population. Before the war, Croats lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that also in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac that there is this village called Srednja Slatina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The majority population in Srednja Slatina, was it also Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Srednja Slatina, the ratio may have been about 65 or 70 per cent of Croats and the rest were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: While you were in Orasje, did you have any contacts with any inhabitants of the villages Kornica and Srednja Slatina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean while I was in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You have some close relatives in Srednja Slatina, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is quite clear. You know that I was born there, I grew up there, and my parents were there, so I don't have some relatives; I do have relatives there indeed. You're not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did they go to Orasje at a certain time from Srednja Slatina? Were you able to rejoin them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. None of my close relatives came to Orasje. They were all either in Croatia or in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether those relatives of yours -- or when your relatives left Srednja Slatina? Was it perhaps in late June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but it may have been in July. I don't know when they left it. I do know that they did leave Slatina, then they spent some time in a territory near Gradacac, and then they went out via Split. The only thing I know, that when I was exchanged, my mother was still in the territory of the then Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean Gradacac? That would be the territory of the Muslim-Croat Federation, because Gradacac was under their control.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in a village called Spionica. That's a village located between Gradacac and Srebrenik, on the Tuzla-Orasje road, and some people stayed there up until a year or two ago. That's a Croat village, and that's where they stayed. As regards my close family and relatives, after July 1992 nobody remained in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fine. Sir, let us move on to another topic. You do have knowledge of a meeting that was held in Prud on the 23rd of March, 1992? The meeting was attended by certain persons, certain officials of the HDZ and the SDA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have some knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did it take place on or about the 23rd of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the date, I really don't know. I do know that a meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, do you remember whether that was in late March 1992? The exact date is not important. Let me -- if you know that, that would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember what month it was or what date. I just know that it took place in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was it before the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Sulejman Tihic present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He was the president of the municipal board of the SDA in Samac, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Alija Fitozovic present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I don't object to the question, but I think that what should be established first of all is whether this witness was at the meeting, so that we know whether he's talking -- using first-hand knowledge or whether he's telling us something that was reported to him. Because it's not yet clear if this man was actually there or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pantelic, I think you can find out that from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Maybe it can be useful. But, well, I think it's irrelevant. It's irrelevant for the following reasons: Maybe this witness heard from someone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, let's not waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, were you present.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have my line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you stop talking?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in Prud at the time, but I wasn't present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. You can proceed, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether Alija Fitozovic was at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Izet Izetbegovic was present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Filip Evic present there? He was the president of the HDZ of the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Mato Nujic present there? He was a Croat, president of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Mato Madzuric [As interpreted] present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean Mato Madzarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There was a typing error. Mato Madzarevic. Thank you for your correction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Stjepan Blazanovic present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't know who that person is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's go on. Was Marko Bozanovic at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Vinko Dragicevic at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Mijo Mijic at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you perhaps mean the teacher from Grebnice?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly: What do you know about the purpose of the meeting and what was going on at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to tell you, and I will. They were in a community hall in Prud, upstairs. I saw Filip Evic, Izet Izetbegovic, and Sulejman Tihic. Upstairs in that room there were some locals who played dominos and watched TV. I was downstairs with some other people from Prud. I can't recall their names now, who they were. And I think that this meeting did not last long, and I will tell you why. At that time, Izetbegovic - I mean Izet Izetbegovic - was quite drunk at the time, and I know that down there, in front of the library or the building, that he was discussing politics, so that I don't know whether they did come to an agreement. I do know that at that time, Sulejman Tihic held the function of the president of the party; Izet Izetbegovic was the deputy of the chairman of the executive board of the Samac municipality. He was there as a representative of the SDA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the question is not being answered. The question was: "Do you know what the purpose of the meeting was?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you hear later on that the formation of the joint Crisis Staff of the SDA and the HDZ was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And as far as I know, while I was in Samac, no staff, no joint staff of Croats and Muslims, was ever established in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But was there an idea to establish a joint staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The witness has said he doesn't know. He's asked that question directly, very, very clearly by Mr. Pantelic: "Did you later hear that the formation of the joint Crisis Staff of the SDA was discussed at the meeting?" Answer: "No. And as far as I know, while I was in Samac, no staff, no joint staff, was ever established." So no, he didn't hear anything about it, and he said no, he doesn't know what the purpose of the meeting is. End of story.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's, I would say, two actions. One action is whether this Crisis Staff was established, and the other pair of shoes is whether this witness, up to this particular date, heard something about the possible initiative to establish such a Crisis Staff. Because he said that at that time he was not aware. Now I'm asking him, up to this moment, whether he had certain personal knowledge about the initiatives for that. So it's rather a different question that my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean you're trying to find out from the witness whether after the incident of the meeting, whether he heard later on that there was such a plan to establish a joint Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is correct. And up until today, actually, in various --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. You can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- opportunities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Witness A, I'm asking you: To this day, since you are moving around in that area, you are talking about people, have you ever heard about this initiative to set up this joint Crisis Staff of the SDA and the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell us: Do you know, since you were a member of the reserve police force in Bosanski Samac, about the arrival of a unit of the special police from Sarajevo, from the BH MUP, before the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did that unit of the special police come to Samac from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it was not a special unit of the Ministry of the Interior from Sarajevo. It was a certain number of police officers who came from various places in what was then Bosnia and Herzegovina. Some came from Tuzla, some came from Zenica, from Vitez, Travnik Sarajevo, I think even from Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So it was a combined or a joint police force that was called "the special police force"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this force was called. I do know, however, that they arrived there on the orders of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was their task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came there with the task to secure facilities of vital importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did their equipment and weapons differ from those that the regular police had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had nothing special. They had the regular uniforms, because they were members of the police -- of the active police force. The only thing that could be seen, that was noticeable, was that some of them had flak jackets. I didn't notice anything out of the ordinary that they had. And let me just say that their immediate superiors came together with them. In that police formation, there were Croats, Muslims, and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were they armed with automatic rifles, Kalashnikov-type?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. However, I think that all of them were armed with automatic rifles manufactured by Crvene Zastava. They had the same weapons that we members of Bosanski Samac police had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did they have helmets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Those rifles produced by Crvene Zastava were, in fact, domestic versions of Kalashnikov; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I object. What's the relevance of the question? The witness has already said the only thing that was different about these fellows was that they had flak jackets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's the end of it, and it matters not what sort of -- whether they were the domestic version of a Kalashnikov or not. He said the rifles were the same as the ones they carried.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you look a little bit better, page 19, line 10, 11, and 12, he said that they were armed with these automatic rifles. So my question is to clarify whether this type of automatic rifle was actually the former Yugoslav version of Kalashnikov, simple as that. Just for clarification of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just had to clarify some technical matters. Since you just told us that you had an automatic rifle manufactured by Crvene Zastava, and now I'm asking you about the weapons which these special police force members had, are we, in fact, talking about the automatic rifle produced by Crvene Zastava, which is identical to Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know they had the same weapons as we did, and Kalashnikov is something different. Let me tell you this as well: In case you don't know, all members of police, during their service in the police, had, in addition to small weapons, also rifles, which is what that weapon was. This is how it was in all MUP stations in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now that you say "these rifles," you, in fact, are referring to automatic rifles, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did that police unit have special Land Rover vehicles as part of its equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember very well now, but in addition to vehicles that we had at our disposal - and we did not have many - this unit that came in was brought to Samac in vehicles, and those who drove them to Samac went back in their vehicles. I think that one or two Land Rovers remained and were used to bring and drive away -- to drive the policemen from the place where they were accommodated, to the police station. The same kind of police vehicles were used in Samac and in Odzak, as well as in Orasje. So this is what these vehicles were used for.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did they have also pinzgauer vehicles as part of their equipment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, perhaps to assist Mr. Pantelic, perhaps the questions could be framed in a more collective way: Did they have helmets, pinzgauers, automatic rifles, Land Rovers, flak jackets, or whatever else he wants to mention, so we can get one quick answer and solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just this question and I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's only one question and I've finished anyway with this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, just answer me with a yes or no, please. Did they have pinzgauers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How many police units came to Samac? How many of those units were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember what was their number, but they were relieved every 15 days, if I'm not mistaken, and I think that there were over 60 of them, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Witness A, since you are an experienced policeman, can you tell us: Who was the commander of those units? From whom did they receive their orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty roster was made every day, and it specified which policemen should go to secure which facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in finding out more details, Witness A. In view of the nature of these units, will you agree with me if I say that they were subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, headquartered in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of the Interior in Sarajevo dispatched them to Samac with their immediate superiors, and they were put at the disposal of the MUP Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You didn't really answer my question. Do you know who -- under whose command these units were? Was it MUP in Sarajevo or the chief of the public security station in Samac? Under whose command were they? Or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were under the command of their immediate superior, who came with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's not waste time. I'm asking you once again, Witness A: Under whose command their immediate superior was. Was it the chief of the public security station in Sarajevo or was it the MUP - I'm sorry - the head of the public security station in Samac or was it the MUP in Sarajevo? Please give me a direct answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying. I don't know under whose command they were. There were inspectors there, policemen, and I don't know who was in charge. I was a plain policeman there. And they remained in contact with the MUP in Sarajevo. They sent them to Samac and then they ordered them to go, to leave Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's turn to another topic, which is the organisation of the TO staff in Samac. Do you know that this municipal TO staff was established sometime before the 17th of April, 1992? Do you know the exact date when that TO staff was established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the TO staff was established in Samac, and that was a few days before the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the establishment of that staff did not pass through the legal procedure, or rather, that there was not a decision of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac specifying that that staff ought to be established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was an assembly decision or not. I think that at that time the assembly, in fact, did not function. All I know is that the appointment or the establishment was ordered by the government, or rather, by the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 27 of your statement of this year, given in July 2002, you say that they were appointed by the Minister of Defence Jerko Doko; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then I can tell from your statement that you had close ties to the Minister of Defence, Jerko Doko, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Jerko Doko before the multiparty elections, because both of us were soccer referees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You assisted with the establishment of the TO, and you practically had this direct contact with Mr. Jerko Doko, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you exactly how it was so that we can cover this as briefly as possible. Sulejman Tihic and some other people - I can't remember their names - told me that there had been a proposal at the municipal level to establish the TO staff in Sarajevo. They asked me whether I could do something about expediting that, because they said I had a colleague of mine there, Jerko Doko. Up until that time, I didn't even know that he held that office. I made a telephone call and got his number in Sarajevo, and I introduced myself to his secretary, asking her whether I could talk to Mr. Doko. She told me that he was at a meeting. I asked her to convey my greetings to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, can you spare us those details? Can we come to the actual point, whether or not you eventually met with this man and what transpired from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't meet that man, because he was in Sarajevo. The secretary took my message.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I mean eventually. Did you eventually come to work with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's move on, Witness A. In your 1994 statement given to the Prosecution, on page 6 of the B/C/S version, ERN number 00637833, you said as follows: "Alija Fitozovic was appointed there by the SDA party, whereas Bozanovic was appointed by the HDZ party." We are now referring to the leading people of this TO staff. Do you remember saying this to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: You were in Djakovo, which is in Croatia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you went there pursuant to the TO staff order to acquire or purchase some uniforms; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you didn't find the appropriate uniforms, so you came back without getting the job done; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had some other tasks to accomplish, but I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What colour were those uniforms that you were supposed to procure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were of no colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you were in contact with some people there in order to procure uniforms of the Croatian army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, listen. Djakovo is in Croatia, so please explain to us: What were you going to find in Djakovo? What kind of uniforms? Hunting, fishing? What kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a conversation there attended by Marko Bozanovic and some other people, including Mr. Vidak Prusina. They asked me whether I could do something about procuring uniforms in Croatia and how much they would cost. They wanted me to find out where could those uniforms be sewn, because he said that he had some money owed to him by the company where he used to work, which was called Hranaprodukt.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to be as brief as possible? Tell me, please: Did you go to procure military uniforms, police uniforms, or uniforms for car mechanics or uniforms for kitchen chefs? What kind of uniforms were you supposed to procure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to inquire about uniforms so that they could be procured later on, and had I found the uniforms, I would have to report back to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question was -- yes. What type of uniforms? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The uniforms were intended for the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were those military uniforms? What colour were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were military uniforms, and I don't know what colour they would have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We finally established this, and it's quite -- it turns out to be quite a simple answer. Witness A, you were present at the meeting on the 13th and 14th of March, when the TO was established, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your 1994 statement, you said that you carried out certain tasks, like a trip that you undertook to Bosanski Brod to procure something. What were you procuring in Bosanski Brod before the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never stated that I went to Bosanski Brod. It could have only referred to that time when I once travelled to Djakovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me read you out an excerpt from your 1994 statement, ERN number 00637833, page 6 of the B/C/S version, where you say the following: "I assisted a little bit with the Territorial Defence regarding the establishment of the TO unit for Bosanski Samac. I carried out tasks, such as travelling to Bosanski Brod to procure something, or I assisted those who were supposed to establish contacts with the higher echelons in Sarajevo." This is something that you stated in 1994, when your memory was a great deal fresher than it is now. Do you still maintain this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Bosanski Brod, in my interviews with the Prosecution, I told them, both on the last occasion and the one before that, that this did not pertain to Bosanski Brod but in fact it had to do with Djakovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have our break? Ms. Reidy, did you want to say anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to object if Mr. Pantelic continued on this, because the witness has said twice, and said quite clearly, that the reference to Bosanski Brod was meant to be a reference to Djakovo. That is indeed what he told me. It was in his draft statement. It's what Mr. Pantelic has and was disclosed to him and the witness has reconfirmed twice to Mr. Pantelic that whatever was put down in his 1994 statement as Bosanski Brod should have read Djakovo. And that was made clear in the draft statement disclosed to Mr. Pantelic after I spoke with this witness and he had a chance to read his statement and correct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall take our break and continue the proceedings at 1720.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We're continuing with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Allow me first to express, on behalf of all Defence teams, our gratitude to the efforts of the Office of the Registrar, particularly Mr. Christian Rohde, and also chief of security, allowing us access to the terrace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You finally got it. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Better than now than in December, but ... Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness A, you mentioned that there was an idea about financing of the uniforms in Djakovo by a company called Hranaprodukt from Djakovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In 1992, Hranaprodukt was a socially owned company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, the funding of the TO was a responsibility of the Ministry of Defence; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your statement given to the Prosecution in July of 2002, in paragraph 33, you stated that you had a flak jacket, a rifle, and a pistol. What I would like to know is what type of a rifle you had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an automatic rifle, manufactured by Crvene Zastava, which I was issued with in MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 40 of that same statement, you said that you had a camouflage uniform that you left in the common room of your building. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that same statement, in paragraph 39, you said that you had two bombs. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I suppose they were hand grenades. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were called Kasikara.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your statement given to the OTP in 1994, last three -- last three ERN numbers are 834. On page 7 of B/C/S version, you said that you had a walkie-talkie. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 40 of your July 2002 statement, you said that you removed your uniform once you realised that there would be no resistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, for the sake of saving time, can -- avoid repeating what is in the statement. Simply go ahead with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will do that, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your 1994 statement to the OTP, you said the following. You were discussing the Good Friday and the festivities, and you said: "I thought that I shouldn't leave until my sister, her husband and children were in town because my goal was to provide resistance." That's what you stated in 1994, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what I stated, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, then: Were you a member of some organised unit that was supposed to provide a joint resistance in case there were some conflicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So what kind of resistance were you supposed to offer, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was supposed to offer resistance in order to protect myself, my apartment, and -- or the place where I am at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your 1994 statement, on page 8 of the B/C/S version, last three ERN numbers are 835, you said that on the 17th of April, you were together with the Bicic brothers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, together with the Bicic brothers and some other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And all of them were members of one other type of an armed formation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, the way the question is framed, it appears that that's -- Mr. Pantelic is putting to the witness there that that was mentioned in the statement. It should be, if it's a direct question, of course, he can ask it, but let's be clear that that's what it is and it's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- a quote from the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have personal knowledge whether the Bicic brothers and the other persons that you saw were in an armed formation, organised armed formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: I was a reserve police officer. I was there as a reserve police officer. The Bicic brothers and Muhamed and I don't know on whose behalf they were there, but there was a person by the name of Hare and another person on behalf of the 4th Detachment, and they also had arms.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they didn't hear the name of the person by the name of Darko. His last name wasn't heard by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the full name be given, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last name of the man called Darko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Darko Dujminovic, Dzanko's son. The other one was Jasarevic, nicknamed Hare. I don't know his -- I don't remember his first name. And the Bicic brothers, Muhamed -- and what's the other one's name? Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your 1994 statement, on page 8 of the B/C/S version, you stated the following: "In the Bicic brothers' house, we stayed there for a few hours had. I sent one of them to Prud across the Bosna River. In the meantime, I called some Croats from Prud to check whether we can get these people out." That's what you stated in 1994 to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards this statement in 1994, I said regarding this statement this year to the OTP that I didn't state that but that this was a wrong translation. This is what this is all about. I was with the Bicic brothers at home, at their home, in front of their home. I wasn't inside their house, and one can see from my balcony their house and also a part of the yard. Then Ivica Pranjic went to Prud, took his wife there and came back, and said that it is possible to pass through Prud.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is what kind of relations did you have with people in Prud and with what people in Prud did you communicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really tell you now who is it that I talked to. All I know is that I called somebody in Prud, because I know everybody in Prud.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were they members of the Prud Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there was a Crisis Staff in Prud, and even if it was, who was its member.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your 1994 statement, on page 7 of the B/C/S version, you said that you called your friend Ivan Nikolic, owner of a small cafe called Rustika, and there, with Alija Fitozovic, Marko Bozanovic, and Dragan Lukac, you met to talk. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now I'm asking you: What was the topic of the conversation with the high-ranking officials of the police and the party that you yourself attended? What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there for a quite short time. I found Dragan there. I don't know whether Alija was there too, and Marko Bozanovic was there. On that day I was in Djakovo. And then I came there to report to Marko about the uniforms, and quite soon it was 7.00 and Marko went to the meeting in the local commune. He said that he was going there for the first time in the capacity of the commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I conclude that you had close contacts with the high-ranking party and police officials in Bosanski Samac. Is my conclusion correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had contacts with all the people, from all the parties, not only from the two parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Again in 1994, on page 13 of the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that statement before me. You've been reading from that statement to me for the past hour and a half and I don't have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Copy of witness statement from 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the Serbo-Croat version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, B/C/S version, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 12 of that statement - I'm sorry - page 13 of that statement, you talk about the discussions with Inspector Milos Savic. In your statement, you speak about the fact that he asked you about who had weapons in Srednja Slatina, who was procuring weapons from Croatia, and so on and so forth. You can see that in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You stated that to the OTP at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As regards the question who was importing rifles from Croatia for Bosnian Muslims, you said to Inspector Milos Savic that Namik Suljic and Ragib Hodzic were organising those activities. They were police inspectors from Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What function did Namik Suljic have in the public security station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just to ensure that the record is clear and there's no misleading left on the record, could Mr. Pantelic please make clear that when he then puts to him that the response to Mr. Savic, that it was Namik Suljic and Mr. Hodzic, I don't believe that that is in the statement. That's something else he's just putting to him that was his response. It's not something that he says that this witness said in 1994. So again we're getting -- he says, "you said this in your statement," and then follows up with another question, creating the impression that he's asking the witness to confirm an earlier statement, and that's not in fact the case. So I'd just like again to be clear. If the witness said that it was Namik Suljic and Hodzic, and the witness said it's possible, that is not -- that is Mr. Pantelic's allegation and not a quotation from the witness's 1994 statement, unless Mr. Pantelic can correct me and show me where it is, because I don't see it there and I don't recall it being there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will read from your statement, and please verify whether I'm reading correctly. It's at the end of the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The problem could be solved really quickly if my learned friend could tell us where it is in the English, then we won't object if we can see it. Is it just that we get directed to this and we're desperately looking, scanning the pages trying to see where it is and we can't see it. We may be wrong, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which paragraph in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, there is no numbering of paragraphs. That might be a problem. I have only ERN number of B/C/S version which last three digits are 840, and my learned friends just advised me that it's page 13 of English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The paragraph beginning --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In English version it should be paragraph 3, and I will just read that to the witness and then he can confirm.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Then I can confirm that I see those two names mentioned there, but it's not the same episode. The episode where he said -- the episode that was -- the witness was quoted and it said, "You were asked about who was being armed," et cetera, is one episode; and then the whole thing about Namik Suljic is a separate episode.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the witness has testified that he was interrogated at least on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's the second interview, so ... Now I see it. Thank you. And I'm grateful to my learned friend, but it's not the same occasion. The witness said he was interviewed twice, and it's on the second occasion that this business arises. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The business dealing with --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: With Namik Suljic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, I'm not trying to interrupt the flow of my friend's conversation, but if we can't see it, then we're caught in a position of knowing whether to object or not because we can't find it in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe he can read the relevant paragraph so we're all clear what the paragraph contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's quite a longish paragraph, Your Honour, but I will just read this particular part which is of my interest, and of course my learned friends can examine that in re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Witness A, I'm now reading from your statement, your 1994 statement that you gave to the OTP, and you say, at the end of the first paragraph in your version, and please check whether I'm reading correctly, you said to the OTP the following pertaining to this interview with inspector Milos Savic. You said the following: "He asked me, in other words Milos Savic asked me, who was importing rifles from Croatia for Bosnian Muslims? I told him that all this was organised by Namik Suljic, Ragib Hodzic, and police inspectors from Sarajevo." Did I read correctly what is stated in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did read it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So my question now is -- well, there is a problem with the transcript, and I apologise to the interpreters, and I will now repeat it for the transcript: "He asked me who was importing rifles for Bosnian Muslims from Croatia. I told him that all that was organised by Namik Suljic and Ragib Hodzic, police inspectors from Sarajevo." And now my question to you is: Namik Suljic had some kind of a function in the police station in Samac, did he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, sir: I today do not remember what Mr. Savic had asked me in MUP. I was all swollen. I was beaten up. At that time I would have told him that my father had brought that there and not these two people. And I will tell you what Namik was and what Hodzic was, and I stated in my statement - this is not translated correctly. I said it because I knew that Hodzic was in Sarajevo. You have to take into consideration the state that I was in. I think that I, as a witness, am so fair and that I'm really saying things the way they were. You can see yourself that I'm not going into details regarding some issues. And please, if you continue asking such questions, I really will not be able to control myself any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Witness A, I personally have a lot of understanding for everything that you have gone through. I'm not asking you about that. This is an established fact here. I understand you fully. I understand the state that you were in, all the things that you went through. Unfortunately, this happened --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes, but it happened to me, not to you, so how can you then act in this way towards me? This is really sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness A, it's understandable that you went through all the things that you have discussed in your statement, but counsel has to cross-examine on behalf of his client. So please be patient and simply answer the questions. And Mr. Pantelic, perhaps you can reorganise your cross-examination so that you wind up as quickly as possible. We are all aware of the health condition of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm extremely mindful about these conditions. No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness A --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, do not ask me any more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you gave this statement to the OTP of the Tribunal. This is not what you stated to Milos Savic. This is what you said in 1994, on the 8th, 9th, and 10th of October, and the 6th of December, in the presence of Ms. Nancy Paterson and Ms. Maria Velikonja. So this is part of the statement that you gave to the Prosecution. We're not talking about the statements that you gave to Milos Savic. I'm asking you a very short and clear question: What function Namik Suljic had. Could you please just tell me that? It's very simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I've got the statement in front of me and I've been hoping that I clarify this business in re-examination so that you and the witness will know exactly in what context this name of Namik Suljic was mentioned. Now, it's really quite unfair to the witness to be focusing on that particular phrase and sentence. Mr. Pantelic has failed to take the witness to what precedes that particular phrase and sentence regarding Namik Suljic. He has failed to mention that the witness has clearly stated in the statement just above, just above, that Savic was insisting on a list of names of people who possessed guns. He gave him a list of names of people who he was certain was not there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He put his brother Pero's name on the list because he knew he wasn't there, and he was offering these names in order to placate his interrogators, and it's obvious from reading the statement that that's what he was doing, and that's how these names Suljic and Hodzic arise. What Mr. Pantelic is doing is taking these names completely out of context and failing to put the previous part. The witness was feeding them false information to keep his torturers happy. That's what you understand from reading the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that explanation. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I'm wrong, but this is a cross-examination based on adversarial system. I said, prior to this line of questioning, that I'm focusing on the topics when this witness discussed certain issues when he was being interrogated by the Inspector Milos Savic. I'm not -- I don't have intention to read, because of the problem of timing, to read all paragraphs. Sufficiently, I put him on notice that we are speaking, first of all, about his conversation with Inspector Milos Savic, about the topics, a gist from his statement to the Prosecution, and then I'm going to explore certain particular question which might be not in direct relation with this particular witness, but since we have our defence case, we have to cover many areas, maybe I want to clarify certain things with regard to the other witnesses and testimony. This is a defence case and this is cross-examination. And I really kindly ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- to relax and -- to relax and to wait his time for re-direct for clarification, Your Honour. I don't see anything which is not in accordance with the standards of cross-examination and with the procedure before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But the point explained by Mr. Di Fazio that matters should not be taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, they're not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- when read from the statement which the witness made --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- Is a correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just give introduction, as I said, that is in transcript here a couple of pages ago. I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We are speaking about the interrogation by Milos Savic, inspector, we are speaking about the topics that he interrogated this witness, and now a part of this statement which this witness gave to the Prosecution, not to Milos Savic. And I tried to explore certain very, very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you are now asking him about the statement he gave to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To the Prosecutor, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The whole time I'm doing that. I don't have any references to any other statements that he gave to the police officer Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Witness A, what function did Namik Suljic have in the Samac police station?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer. Due to technical problems, we didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the deputy or the assistant, but at any rate, he was in the regular police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's just clear this up. He was in the active force. He was the assistant to the commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he the commander of the reserve force in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was the deputy or the assistant to the commander of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the reserve police force in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Namik Suljic is of Muslim ethnic origin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he an SDA member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This police inspector from Sarajevo, Ragib Hodzic, he was an instructor, he was the commander of the special units from Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you answered Milos Savic about the arming of Croats, did you provide him with information about who had weapons in Srednja Slatina, which persons were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first mentioned my brother, and all the houses to the right and to the left of the road, and I really don't know whether at that time they had weapons or not. And let me tell you, sir: If you held 40- or 50-Kilo stone on your knee and if you had to lift up that stone up with your hands up in the air and if they were beating you up at the time you would tell them everything, including the things you didn't know. Before the interrogation conducted by Milos Savic, I had to give the same kind of statements to all kinds of youngsters from Samac. I could have been their father. They went to school with my children and they forced me to do so in the courtyard of the TO building, and everybody was able to see that. What would you say if something like that happened to you? And if I knew for real who had something, I would have said that, and I would have said that in front of this Tribunal in order for the justice to be done, because those who are responsible should be convicted and those who are not should be released. I said voluntarily, told them about the two grenades that I had and about the uniforms that I went for in Djakovo. I don't have to lie about anything. That's how it was. And I really don't know anything else. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a very brief question. The Croats in the Croatian villages in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, before the 17th of April, did they get armed? Did the Croats in villages have weapons? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. And let me explain --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Don't, please. It is, I think, in your own interests for us to finish as soon as possible, so let's try to finish. The Croats in the Croat villages in the Bosanski Samac municipality, before the 17th of April, 1992, did they organise checkpoints and guards, guard duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that in the house of Josip Orsolic, your neighbour and friend, that the Crisis Staff for Domaljevac was located there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was the headquarters for the Croatian Crisis Staff in Domaljevac in the vicinity of Josip Orsolic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which house it was. I know approximately where it was, but it wasn't in the vicinity of Josip's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where was it, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In another house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In which village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that village that you asked me about, but it wasn't the Crisis Staff. I'm saying just that in 1993, when I came to that area, it was not the Crisis Staff. At that time a unit of the Croatian Defence Council had already been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the period before the 17th of April, 1992. Where was the headquarters of the Croatian Crisis Staff for Domaljevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 9 of your 1994 statement given to the OTP. I will read out the beginning of the third paragraph, and you can follow it. You said to the Prosecutor in 1994 as follows: "Stevo Todorovic extended his hand to me." We are now referring to the episode when you were brought into the MUP. So: "Stevo Todorovic extended his hand to me. He greeted me and asked me about my wife and children. He handed me the phone and told me to call Djakovo, where, according to him, I shot at the barracks during the war in Croatia. He told me to tell them" -- he's probably referring to your family here -- "that I would stay there for some time. I told him that I had nobody to call there, and he then sent me upstairs. He used Serb phrases. He said he wouldn't let anybody touch me and that I was a first-rate member of the HDZ. I thought that that was a sign that they should start beating me. When I got into the building, Stevo Todorovic was chewing the gum, based on which I concluded that he was the one who had called me previously." Is that what is stated in your 1994 statement to the OTP? Did I read out well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the translation I think was not correct on line 7. He said, "Don't let anybody beat him. He's a first or premier-league member of the HDZ," based on which I got the impression that that was the sign that they should start beating me. Prior to my arrest, I was in the corridor, because there had been an announcement that nobody should move about, and then the phone rang. I picked up the phone and I simply heard that somebody was chewing gum. And then the person on the other side put the receiver down. A few minutes later, these two guys came to fetch me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So basically what you stated in 1994 is correct. You maintain what you said in your 1994 statement to the OTP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
